quote: Thinking of this, secretly I grew ashamed; / And all day the thought lingered in my head.
source: Bai Juyi, Watching the Reapers, the closing two lines, p. 41, More Translations from the Chinese (trans. Arthur Waley, 1919)
note: Corrected the locator. Watching the Reapers is poem 15 of the whole volume, not the fifteenth poem of the Po Chu-i section, where it stands fifth. The source now cites page 41 of More Translations from the Chinese, Knopf, 1919. Waley prints the poet as Po Chu-i and dates the poem A.D. 806. The wording is exact.

evidence.where: The Project Gutenberg transcription of the 1919 Knopf edition, read in full: the contents page puts Watching the Reapers at page 41 inside the PO CHÜ-I section, and the poem itself is headed [15] WATCHING THE REAPERS with the bracketed date A.D. 806.
evidence.edition: More Translations from the Chinese, trans. Arthur Waley (Alfred A. Knopf, 1919)
evidence.locator: PO CHÜ-I section, p. 41, poem 15 of the volume, the closing two lines

reason: The two closing lines are exact in Waley, semicolon and all, and the poem is a salaried officer ashamed of his own ease beside the reapers. Only the locator needed work: the number 15 counts poems across the whole book, while the poem is the fifth of the Po Chu-i group, so the page carries the citation instead.
